title: Yamada Denki says its reform management system was accessed without authorisation; customer data may have leaked
date_note: NHK (13 Nov) and ScanNetSecurity report the company announced the incident on 13 November; the company says it found the access on 12 November.
summary: According to NHK and ScanNetSecurity, Yamada Denki said its reform management system was accessed without authorisation, which the company confirmed on 12 November. Names, addresses, phone numbers and renovation history may have been affected, in up to 3.5 million records, and ScanNetSecurity adds estimate data. The company says it blocked external access and is still investigating the scope and cause.
plain: Yamada Denki says its renovation management system was accessed without authorisation and customer details may have been affected, in up to 3.5 million records. It is still investigating.
exec: Up to 3.5 million possibly affected Yamada Denki customer records raise impersonation and fraud risk for its customers.
action: General advice: Yamada Denki customers should treat unexpected calls, messages or emails claiming to be from the company with caution.
impact: Up to 3.5 million records possibly affected; number of people not stated.

validation.note: Corroborated by NHK, ScanNetSecurity and Security NEXT, independent publishers that each state the unauthorised access and the up-to-3.5-million figure. The company notice itself was not opened.

review.note: Compared with Security NEXT (20 Nov): found 12 Nov, up to 3.5 million records, data types, access cut off, cause under investigation all match. Exec said 'major Japanese retailer', not on the page; now names the company only. Remains single_source.
